skills.summary: Prove work meets its acceptance conditions
skills.job: Prove the work meets its acceptance conditions with fresh evidence before claiming it is done
triggers: are we done, verify it
check that this actually works before you say finished
prove it meets the requirements
gotchas: reporting a test run from before the last edit
checking the code path you wrote instead of the condition the user stated
treating a green build as proof of behaviour

skills.summary: Respond to review comments and apply them
skills.job: Work through reviewer comments one by one, apply the valid ones, and push back with evidence on the rest
triggers: address the review comments on my PR
reviewer asked for changes, handle them
reply to this code review feedback
gotchas: applying every comment literally including ones that conflict
fixing the quoted line but not the same pattern elsewhere
replying done without saying what changed

skills.summary: Review your own diff before asking others
skills.job: Read your own diff as a stranger would and fix what a reviewer would flag before opening the pull request
triggers: review my diff before I open the PR
self review my changes
what would a reviewer flag in my branch
gotchas: reading the files instead of the diff so leftovers stay hidden
skipping debug prints and commented code because you remember adding them
reviewing only what you meant to change

skills.summary: Review identifiers for clarity and consistency
skills.job: Audit names of variables, functions, files and types for accuracy and consistency with the codebase vocabulary
triggers: review the naming in this module
are these names clear
find misleading names in my code
gotchas: suggesting names that clash with the project's existing vocabulary
renaming a public name without checking external callers
flagging short names in tiny scopes where they are fine

skills.summary: Find swallowed, leaked and misreported errors
skills.job: Review how code detects, propagates, reports and recovers from failures, and list the paths that lose or hide errors
triggers: review the error handling here
what happens when this fails
find swallowed exceptions
gotchas: counting a catch that logs and continues as handled
checking only the happy-path callers of a throwing function
accepting retry loops with no limit or backoff

skills.summary: Review code for shared-state and ordering hazards
skills.job: Review a change for shared mutable state, lock use, ordering assumptions and cancellation problems before it ships
triggers: review this for thread safety
is this async code safe
check locking and shared state in this change
gotchas: trusting that a single-threaded runtime means no interleaving across awaits
approving a lock without checking every path that touches the data
missing that cancellation leaves state half-updated

skills.summary: Find code nothing calls and prove it is dead
skills.job: Find unused functions, exports, files and flags and prove each is unreachable before proposing deletion
triggers: find dead code in this project
what can I delete safely
list unused exports
gotchas: missing dynamic references such as string lookups and reflection
treating exports used only by tests as dead or as live without saying so
deleting what a plugin or config file loads by path

skills.summary: Locate the code that is hardest to change
skills.job: Rank files and functions by complexity and churn to show where refactoring pays off first
triggers: where is the most complex code
find hotspots in this repo
what should we refactor first
gotchas: ranking by size alone and ignoring how often a file changes
flagging generated or vendored code
reporting a score without saying what makes the function hard

skills.summary: Detect breaking changes in a public interface
skills.job: Compare an interface before and after a change and list what would break existing callers or consumers
triggers: is this a breaking change
will this break our API consumers
check backwards compatibility of this diff
gotchas: calling an added required field non-breaking
ignoring behaviour changes behind an unchanged signature
forgetting serialised formats, error codes and defaults as part of the contract

skills.summary: Tune lint rules to fit the codebase
skills.job: Adjust a linter configuration so it catches real problems with few false positives and no churn
triggers: our linter is too noisy
tune the eslint config
which lint rules should we enable
gotchas: enabling a rule repo-wide and creating thousands of fixes in one commit
disabling a rule instead of fixing the few real hits
changing config without running the linter before and after

skills.summary: Record and rank technical debt items
skills.job: Capture technical debt as dated, costed ledger entries with a trigger for paying each one
triggers: track our tech debt
write down the shortcuts we took
prioritise the debt in this repo
gotchas: entries that say what is ugly but not what it costs
a ledger with no owner or review date that rots
listing every TODO as debt

skills.summary: Language-specific review checks for a diff
skills.job: Pick the review checks that matter for the language and framework of the change and apply them to the diff
triggers: what should I look for in this Python PR
review this Go code for common mistakes
checklist for reviewing TypeScript changes
gotchas: applying one language's idioms to another
quoting rules from memory that the project's linter or version has changed
using a generic checklist when the project has its own conventions

skills.summary: Make code easier to read without changing it
skills.job: Do a bounded pass that improves reading flow of code through comments, ordering and small clarifications, behaviour unchanged
triggers: make this code easier to read
do a readability pass
this function is hard to follow
gotchas: restructuring logic under the label of readability
adding comments that restate the code
reformatting a whole file and burying the real diff

skills.summary: Review log statements for signal and safety
skills.job: Review log calls for usefulness at 3 a.m., correct levels, context and leaked secrets or personal data
triggers: review the logging in this change
are we logging the right things
check logs for sensitive data
gotchas: logging a request body that holds tokens or personal data
error logs without the identifier needed to find the failing record
logging the same failure at every layer it passes through

skills.summary: Rank the files in a diff by review risk
skills.job: Sort a large diff into what needs careful reading, what needs a skim and what is mechanical
triggers: this PR is huge, where do I start
triage this diff
which changes are risky
gotchas: spending the effort on the largest file instead of the riskiest
trusting that a rename-only file contains only renames
missing config, migration and lockfile changes buried among source files
